excerpts.text: The [Nobel Prize in Physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize_in_Physics "Nobel Prize in Physics") ([Swedish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_language "Swedish language"): _Nobelpriset i fysik_) is awarded annually by the [Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Swedish_Academy_of_Sciences "Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences") to scientists in the various fields of [physics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics "Physics"). It is one of the five [Nobel Prizes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Prize "Nobel Prize") established by the 1895 [will](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_and_testament "Will and testament") of [Alfred Nobel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Nobel "Alfred Nobel") (who died in 1896), awarded for outstanding contributions in physics.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-1) As dictated by Nobel's will, the award is administered by the [Nobel Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Foundation "Nobel Foundation") and awarded by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-2) The award is presented in [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm") at an annual ceremony on 10 December, the anniversary of Nobel's death.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-3) Each recipient receives a medal, a diploma and a monetary award prize that has varied throughout the years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates_in_Physics#cite_note-4)
